subject: Clarification: affirmation we won't use customer text for model training + retention/delete edge cases
messages:
From: Alice Kim <alice.kim@finco.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finco.com, security@finco.com
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify: We need a clear statement that Redwood does not train models on customer text

Hi Stephanie,

Following up from our vendor review this morning — FinCo's security and procurement teams want a concise, auditable statement we can put in our vendor binder that explains: 1) whether Redwood ever uses customer-provided text to train base or fine-tuned models; 2) where customer data is retained (including backups/snapshots) and for how long; and 3) the practical deletion flow (what happens to logs, KV cache, snapshot artifacts, and backups when we request deletion).

A couple of clarifying points for our legal folks: they want language on exceptions (e.g., aggregated telemetry, PII removal efforts) and on the retention of diagnostic snapshots that may be stored for incident analysis. Also confirm whether there's any scenario where derivative model artifacts could be generated that include customer text.

Can you point us to the evidence pack and give a short summary we can include in the binder?

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Kim
Security Program Manager, FinCo

---
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alice Kim <alice.kim@finco.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com, procurement@finco.com, security@finco.com
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 20:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: We need a clear statement that Redwood does not train models on customer text

Alice —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: Redwood does not use customer-provided text to train our public or private model catalog by default, and we offer contractual commitments and technical controls to enforce that for customers who require it. Below I attach an evidence pack and a one-page assertion that you can drop into your binder.

High-level bullets for procurement/legal:
- No training on customer text: By default, customer requests and content are routed to inference only. We do not add customer inputs to our model training pipelines.
- Scoped exception: Aggregated, anonymized telemetry (usage metrics, anonymized token counts) are collected for product improvement; we will not surface customer plaintext back into any model training.
- Backups & snapshots: Production request logs are retained per the retention settings of the account's region and plan. Snapshots used for debugging are short-lived by default (30 days) and are tombstoned prior to deletion; long-term snapshots require explicit ops approval.
- Deletion flow: Data erasure request triggers: 1) tombstone primary records; 2) remove from live KV caches and invalidate caches; 3) schedule deletion from backups/snapshots subject to region-specific retention windows (typically 90 days for backups in EU deployments); 4) confirm deletion and provide deletion receipts.
- No derivative training: We do not create derivative (customer-specific) models from customer content unless explicitly contracted (customer-owned fine-tuning). Any such work is done in isolated environments with customer agreement.

I'll let Marissa provide the technical appendices (where logs live, how snapshots are isolated, and the playbook for deletion). Attaching: redwood_nontraining_evidence.pdf (one-page assertion + audit pointers) and delete-playbook-v1.docx (ops playbook).

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Kim <alice.kim@finco.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 11 Dec 2027 07:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify: We need a clear statement that Redwood does not train models on customer text

Hi Alice — adding a few technical specifics to back up Stephanie's summary. I want to be explicit about the components you mentioned.

1) Request ingestion & inference path
- Customer inputs are accepted by the request gateway and forwarded to the inference runtime. We maintain per-customer namespaces; no automated process exists that copies raw request payloads into our training data repositories.

2) Caching & KV artifacts
- KV caches are ephemeral per-run and persisted only when the customer config opts in (session restore). We provide controls to disable session persistence. When deletion is requested we invalidate keys and scrub persisted cache files.

3) Debug snapshots & incident artifacts
- Debug snapshots are retained for 30 days by default in the customer's region. They are stored in an encrypted snapshot store with separate ACLs. For EU-hosted accounts the snapshot TTL cannot exceed 90 days without Engineering approval. Snapshots are tombstoned (metadata flagged) prior to secure deletion; tombstone records remain to track deletion workflows but contain no plaintext.

4) Backups & archives
- Backups are regular block-storage snapshots orchestrated by the infra team. Depending on the deployment type (hosted vs dedicated vs private), backups may be customer-controlled (Private) or Redwood-managed (Hosted/Dedicated). For hosted accounts in the EU, the standard backup retention is 90 days; we can shorten it contractually.

5) Telemetry & aggregated metrics
- We collect anonymized telemetry (request counts, latency histograms, tokenization ratios) for product improvement. We do not retain per-request plaintext in telemetry streams.

6) Deletion receipts & attestation
- After the delete workflow completes, we produce a cryptographically signed deletion receipt that lists the artifacts removed and the retention windows that were honored or truncated. The receipt includes reference IDs for snapshots/backups and a timestamp.

If FinCo needs a stricter timeline (e.g., 30-day max for all artifacts), we can add a contractual addendum and implement the shorter TTL in the EU region.

- Marissa
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: delete-playbook-v1.docx

---
From: security@finco.com <security@finco.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finco.com, alice.kim@finco.com
Date: Sat, 11 Dec 2027 17:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify: We need a clear statement that Redwood does not train models on customer text

Stephanie/Marissa —

Thanks for the fast, thorough responses and the evidence pack. A couple of follow-ups before we add the assertion to the binder:

1) Can you confirm whether ephemeral debug snapshots ever leave the EU region (e.g., if an engineer in the US pulls a snapshot for debugging)? We need assurance that no plaintext crosses regions without our consent.

2) For the deletion receipt, will you include the hash of the deleted artifacts and a timestamp (we require tamper-evident receipts)?

3) If we opt into a contractual 30-day TTL, we want to verify there is an automated enforcement path (not a manual ops ticket) — can you commit to automation in your implementation timeline?

If you can confirm these three items, procurement will proceed to finalize the SOW and we'll include the one-page assertion.

Regards,
FinCo Security
